name: Tobiah
bio: Tobiah, an Ammonite official, was furious with Sanballat when he heard Nehemiah had come to seek Israel's welfare, and later mocked the Jews with Sanballat and Geshem the Arab as rebels against the king when they began rebuilding Jerusalem's wall. Nehemiah told them God would prosper the work and that they had no share, right, or claim in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 2:10, 19-20). His continued opposition is told in detail in the chapters ahead. When the Jews kept building despite his scoffing that a fox could knock down their wall, Tobiah joined other peoples in conspiring to attack Jerusalem and halt the work, a plot Nehemiah foiled by posting an armed watch (Nehemiah 4:1-15). He and Sanballat hired Shemaiah son of Delaiah and the prophetess Noadiah to try to frighten Nehemiah into fleeing or sinning, without success; the wall was finished in fifty-two days despite their schemes. Tied to many of Judah's nobles by marriage — his father-in-law was Shechaniah son of Arah, and his son Johanan had married Meshullam son of Berechiah's daughter — Tobiah kept sending letters to unsettle Nehemiah even after the wall stood (Nehemiah 6:10-19). While Nehemiah was away, Tobiah, through his ally Eliashib the priest, had secured a large storeroom chamber in the temple itself; when Nehemiah returned, he threw out all of Tobiah's belongings and had the room purified (Nehemiah 13:4-9).
